newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine 91-day T-bill yield rises to 10.777 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine 91-day T-bill yield rises to 10.777 pct.

text.p: The yield on the Philippine 91-day treasury bill rose to 10.777 percent at the weekly auction on Monday, the Bureau of Treasury said.
Last week, the yield was at 10.356 percent.
The yield on the 182-day bills rose to 11.076 percent from 10.597 while the one year-bills went up to 11.511 percent from the previous 11.088.
The higher rates came after the Central Bank raised its benchmark overnight borrowing rate to 15 percent from 12.75 percent late last week to ward off a speculative attack on the Philippine peso.
"Rates were higher than expected. The market is speculating because of the Thai baht," Treasurer Caridad Valdehuesa told reporters after the auction.
She said banks had placed their funds in the foreign exchange market following the volatility last Friday. As of mid-session Monday, a total of $207 million had been traded.
Tenders were small especially for the three-month bills, with only 2.87 billion pesos worth of tenders received for the 91-day bills. The auction committee accepted 1.5 billion pesos worth of bids.

Tenders for the 182-day bills totalled 4.585 billion pesos, while bids for the 364-day bills were worth 6.650 billion. The committee awarded 1.5 billion pesos for the six-month bills and 2.0 billion pesos for the one-year bills.
Valdehuesa said the Treasury was expecting only a 35 basis point increase for the bellwether 91-day T-bills.
The committee was expecting a 42 basis point rise for the six-month bills, and a 31 basis point hike for the one-year bills.
